title: Trains to operate normally as strike called off
byline: Railway services will operate as normal today (10) after railway controllers called off the trade union action that was scheduled to commence at midnight yesterday (09).

title: Provincial Council elections will be held only after amending electoral system: Harini
byline: Ruling out the possibility of holding the Provincial Council elections under the proportional representation system, Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya told Parliament today that the polls will be held only after introducing a new electoral system.

title: Father of two shot dead after entering cashew estate
byline: A 36-year-old father of two was shot dead after he and a group of villagers entered a cashew plantation in Wanathawilluwa to collect fallen cashew nuts, prompting police investigations and the arrest of eight suspects.

title: No decision to extend retirement age of judges: Minister
byline: Amidst controversy over reports of the extension of retirement age of judges, Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said yesterday that the government has not taken any decision, claiming that there has been no discussion on the matter within the government.

title: Sallay’s treatment could be meted out to others in the Opposition: UNP
byline: The United National Party (UNP) while highlighting that the treatment meted out to former State Intelligence Services (SIS) Chief Major General Suresh Sallay in violation of the Constitution and international conventions, said the treatment meted out to Sallay may be applied on other opposition groups.

title: Sri Lankan doctor found guilty of sexually touching female patient in Perth
byline: A Sri Lankan immigrant doctor has been found guilty of indecently assaulting a female patient during an acupuncture appointment in Perth.

title: Enthusiasm among local, foreign investors galore to take Mattala airport
byline: With as many as 47 parties initially responding to the call for Expressions of Interest (EOI) for the development of the Mattala International Airport (MIA), which is a strategic asset being eyed by countries involved in geopolitical contestation, the authorities have extended the deadline by one more month at the request of participants, an official said yesterday.

title: Millions including NDB monies siphoned out of Sri Lanka under guise of importing goods
byline: While Sri Lanka is grappling with a dollar crisis, investigations conducted by the police and Sri Lanka Customs have uncovered a massive scam where millions of US Dollars including the Rs.13 billion NDB fraud was siphoned out of the country under the guise of importing goods since 2023.

title: Iran’s lakes are vanishing: Satellite images show a deepening water crisis
byline: For many Iranians, the most immediate threat is no longer just war, but water.

title: Nasa names next astronauts for Artemis Moon programme
byline: NASA has named its crew for its next major Moon mission, Artemis III, though the astronauts will not walk on the Moon or go anywhere near it.

title: Iran strikes Bahrain and Jordan in retaliation for US attacks in Hormuz
byline: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has claimed attacks on United States military bases in Bahrain and Jordan in retaliation for US strikes on ports and islands in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: France bans Israel’s finance minister
byline: France on Tuesday banned Israel’s Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich from entry, slamming the far-right politician’s calls for the annexation of the occupied West Bank, new settlements in the area and the “recolonisation” of Gaza. Smotrich was among dozens of Israelis who were slapped with sanctions by France, Britain, Canada, ​Australia, New Zealand and Norway.

title: US-Iran strikes intensify after American patrol helicopter downed in Hormuz
byline: The US and Iran have exchanged fire after the US threatened retaliation for the downing of an American military helicopter over the Iran Strait of Hormuz on Monday that President Donald Trump attributed to Iran.

title: Man arrested for stealing temple studio equipment
byline: A suspect who broke into a recording studio at the Maduluwawa Sri Sudharmarama Temple in Padukka and stole computers and recording equipment worth around Rs. 1.5 million has been arrested by Padukka Police.

title: Sri Lanka now second most peaceful in South Asia: Report
byline: The Institute for Economics & Peace (IEP) has released its 20th annual Global Peace Index (GPI) report for 2026, revealing that Sri Lanka achieved the largest percentage improvement in peacefulness within the South Asia region.

title: Senior DIG seeks court order to prevent arrest over Easter Sunday probe
byline: Senior Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Waruna Jayasundara has filed a writ application before the Court of Appeal seeking an order preventing his arrest without probable cause in connection with the ongoing investigations into the 2019 Easter Sunday terrorist attacks.

title: Fishermen warned of rough seas
byline: The Department of Meteorology has warned of very rough sea conditions and strong winds in several coastal areas around Sri Lanka.

title: Air Canada pilot accused of flying for 17 years without proper licence
byline: A former airline pilot in Canada has been arrested for allegedly flying hundreds of flights without a proper licence for nearly 17 years.

title: Twelve killed in mass shooting in Johannesburg, police say
byline: At least 12 people have been killed in a mass shooting in an area of Johannesburg, police in South Africa say.

title: Rupee strengthens against USD
byline: The Sri Lankan Rupee recorded a notable appreciation against the US Dollar across several commercial banks today (10), compared to Tuesday, with the selling rate falling below Rs. 336 at some banks.

title: Central Bank issues new rules on export earnings conversion
byline: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) has issued an updated regulatory framework governing the repatriation and mandatory conversion of export proceeds, according to an Extraordinary Gazette notification.

title: Some Opposition MPs are brainless: Speaker
byline: Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne, who lost his cool today, accused that some Opposition MPs are brainless.

title: NASA taps US astronauts, Italian for Artemis mission with SpaceX, Blue Origin mooncraft
byline: NASA named three U.S. astronauts and an Italian astronaut on Tuesday to serve as the crew for its next Artemis mission, a spacecraft docking demonstration in Earth’s orbit next year that ​will test moon landers from Elon Musk’s SpaceX and Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin for the first time in space.

title: Speaker threatens to remove MP Sujeewa Senasinghe from chambers
byline: In the midst of a heated argument over Standing Orders pertaining to raising questions, Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne today threatened to have MP Sujeewa Senasinghe removed from the chambers.

title: Kuwait restricts domestic worker recruitment to 10 countries including Sri Lanka
byline: Kuwait’s Interior Ministry has issued a new circular restricting the recruitment of domestic workers to 10 approved countries, while banning recruitment from 27 others, as part of updated regulations governing the domestic labour sector, local media reported.

title: President Anura congratulates Modi on becoming India’s longest-serving elected PM
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has extended warm congratulations to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on becoming the longest-serving elected Prime Minister in the history of India.

title: 12-hour water cut in Mahara and Gampaha for central expressway pipe relocation
byline: Water supply will be temporarily suspended for 12 hours from 7.00 p.m. on Thursday, June 11, 2026, to 7.00 a.m. on Friday (12), due to essential maintenance work linked to the relocation of water pipes for the Central Expressway construction, the National Water Supply and Dranage Board (NWSDB) said.

title: Sri Lanka–Japan UNDP project to aid cyclone Ditwah recovery for over 900,000 people
byline: Around 228,500 people will benefit directly, while a further 700,000 are expected to gain indirect benefits through improved services and strengthened local waste management systems under a new Sri Lanka–Japan recovery initiative supported by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

title: Firms charged with manslaughter over deadly Hong Kong fire
byline: Hong Kong authorities have charged two companies and seven people over the devastating fire at the Wang Fuk housing complex last November.

title: Sri Lanka to inaugurate first boat launching ramp to boost marine industry
byline: The Industries and Entrepreneurship Development Ministry, which is driving initiatives to strengthen Sri Lanka’s emerging boat and boat-related manufacturing sector, will inaugurate the country’s first-ever Boat Launching Ramp tomorrow (11).

title: Court orders five-member medical board to examine Suresh Sallay
byline: Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena today ordered that a report be submitted to the court on July 1 after a five-member medical board comprising three specialist psychiatrists and two Judicial Medical Officers (JMOs) examines whether former State Intelligence Service Director Suresh Sallay, who is currently being detained and questioned under detention orders over the Easter Sunday terror attacks,

title: Satyagraha opposing detention of Suresh Sallay called off
byline: The Satyagraha staged opposite the Colombo Fort Railway Station in protest against the detention of former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director, Major General (Retired) Suresh Sallay, has been called off.

title: BYD chairman says firm will be world’s biggest automaker in 5 years as shares slide
byline: Wang Chuanfu, chairman of BYD , on Tuesday said he expected the Chinese firm to become the world’s largest automaker within five years, as he sought to ​reassure investors following a steep decline in the company’s share price.

title: What Do Sri Lankan Fans Think? Ranking the Top Contenders for the FIFA World Cup 2026
byline: With the FIFA World Cup 2026 fast approaching, Sri Lankan football fans remain divided over who will lift the trophy. A Daily Mirror poll found no clear favourite, with support spread across Spain, France, Argentina, Portugal, England and Brazil.

title: 31,000 premises inspected in dengue drive; 1,864 found with larvae
byline: The Health and Mass Media Ministry has reported significant mosquito breeding risks across the country as part of its ongoing three-day national dengue control programme, with inspections revealing widespread concerns in homes, workplaces, and public institutions.

title: Railway union warns of wider disruptions over ongoing 48-hour strike
byline: The Railway Controllers’ Union has warned authorities not to take the ongoing 48-hour trade union action lightly, cautioning of wider disruptions if the railway work stoppage continues.

title: Pakistani airstrikes kill at least 13 in Afghanistan, Taliban says
byline: At ​least 13 people were killed, including 11 children, ‌after Pakistan’s military launched air strikes in three Afghan provinces, Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid said on Wednesday, in ​a renewal of a conflict that has killed ​hundreds this year.

title: Bribery Commission arrests Shan Wijayalal over chair procurement scam
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has arrested former Chief Minister of the Southern Province Shan Wijayalal De Silva over corruption allegations today.

title: Trump and Iran trade new threats after strikes exchanged
byline: US President Donald Trump and Iran’s senior officials have traded new threats of further action, after the two sides exchanged strikes.

title: ’’Rebuilding Sri Lanka Fund’’ just a name given to Treasury’s DST account: Bimal
byline: Claiming that some Opposition MPs are attempting to mislead the people claiming that there is no fund called ’’Rebuilding Sri Lanka Fund’’, Leader of the House and Minister Bimal Ratnayake said today that the ’’Rebuilding Sri Lanka Fund’’ is just a name given to the account of the Deputy Secretary to the Treasury (DST) and that funds received to the account is credited to the government’s consolidated fund.

title: Luxembourg-backed WEAIR Cargo Airline launched in Sri Lanka
byline: Sri Lanka’s newest cargo airline, WEAIR, officially commenced operations on June 6, 2026, with the launch ceremony held at the Kingsbury Hotel in Colombo under the patronage of Foreign Affairs, Overseas Employment and Tourism Minister, Vijitha Herath.

title: Shan Wijayalal remanded over alleged procurement irregularities
byline: Former Chief Minister of the Southern Province and former Member of Parliament Shan Wijayalal de Silva has been remanded until June 12 by the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court.

title: One student missing after three swept away by waves at Galle Face
byline: Three school students were swept away by strong waves while swimming off the Galle Face beach in Colombo this afternoon (10), prompting a search and rescue operation by the Sri Lanka Navy.

title: CAA imposes new maximum retail prices for bottled drinking water
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has imposed new maximum retail prices (MRPs) for locally packaged and bottled drinking water, effective from today (10).

title: Tamil Nadu leaders mourn Bharathiraja’s demise; state to accord full honours
byline: Veteran filmmaker and actor Bharathiraja, credited with transforming Tamil cinema, died in Chennai on Wednesday at the age of 84 following age-related health issues. His passing has prompted an outpouring of tributes from political leaders and film personalities.

title: Rs. 200 mn allocated to boost women entrepreneurship under 2026 budget
byline: The Women and Child Affairs Ministry has launched a series of initiatives aimed at empowering women from economically disadvantaged communities through entrepreneurship development, with Rs. 200 million allocated under the 2026 Budget for a dedicated Women Empowerment Program.

title: Energy storage systems to be introduced to optimise renewable power use: PM
byline: The government plans to introduce energy storage systems to ensure the optimal utilisation of renewable energy in Sri Lanka’s power sector, Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya told Parliament.

title: Sri Lanka targets 10% entrepreneurship rate by 2030: Minister
byline: Sri Lanka aims to significantly expand its entrepreneurship base, with the government setting an ambitious target to raise the country’s entrepreneurship rate from the current 3.2 percent to 10 percent by 2030, Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Sunil Handunnetthi said.

title: Over 250,000 children dropped out of schools from 2018 to 2024 : PM
byline: Some 267,138 children have dropped out of schools between the years 2018 to 2024, Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya told Parliament today.

title: Man killed in train-three-wheeler collision
byline: A three-wheeler driver was killed after being hit by an express train, travelling from Maradana to Hikkaduwa, at the Ganegama railway crossing in Aluthgama this evening.

title: Man arrested with forged documents in Kotikawatta
byline: An individual was arrested with a vast range of forged documents during a raid condcuted by the Nugegoda Division Crimes Investigation Unit on a house at Maha Buthgamuwa in Kotikawatta.
